newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk police detained a rights activist-composer.
newsitem.headline: Turk police detained a rights activist-composer.

text.p: Turkish police have detained a top musician and human rights activist for producing a documentary film which told the stories of Kurdish journalists killed in southeast Turkey, a human rights official said on Wednesday.
The documentary was broadcast by a Kurdish-language satellite television station, MED TV, based in Britain. The channel is banned in Turkey, but widely watched in the mainly-Kurdish southeast.
Sanar Yurdatapan was taken into custody on Tuesday in Istanbul, Umit Efe of the independent Human Rights Association told Reuters.
"He is accused of being the producer of the documentary film, called Pen. But he was not actually the producer. He only composed the music for it," Yurdatapan's lawyer, Eren Keskin, told Reuters.

Turkey says Med-TV is a mouthpiece for the guerrillas of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), which has been fighting for autonomy or independence from Ankara since 1984. More than 20,000 people have been killed in the fight.
Yurdatapan will be taken to Ankara for questioning by the capital's state security court, the lawyer said.
Yurdatapan is among 99 intellectuals who have been on trial for publishing a book last year that contained articles deemed to contravene Turkey's tough laws on separatism. The trial is continuing.
